questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct decreasing order of boiling point of hydrogen halides is
questions.solution: HF is hydrogen bonded, thus it has highest boiling point. The remaining hydrogen halides are gaseous and their boiling points depend on the van der Waals' forces. Greater the molecule mass, greater will be the van der Waals' forces. Hence higher is the boiling point. Thus, the correct order is $\mathrm{HF}\gt\mathrm{HI}\gt\mathrm{HBr}\gt\mathrm{HCl}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct decreasing order of basicity of hydrides of group- 15 elements is
questions.solution:
In general, the basicity of group 15 hydrides
decreases on moving down the group from $\mathrm{NH}_3$ to $\mathrm{SbH}_3$. This is due to the increasing size of the central atom and the decreasing availability of lone pair for donation. Thus, the correct order of basicity of hydrides is
$\mathrm{NH}_3\gt \mathrm{PH}_3\gt \mathrm{AsH}_3\gt \mathrm{SbH}_3$

$\begin{aligned} 3 \mathrm{AgNO}_3+4 \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow & 3 \mathrm{Ag}+4 \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_3 \\ & +3 \mathrm{HNO}_3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The property of halogens which is not correctly matched is
questions.solution: Down the group, electron gain enthalpies become less and less negative with the increase in the size of the halogen. However, electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{F}$ is less negative than $\mathrm{Cl}$. This is due to small size of F-atom. As a result, there are strong inter electronic repulsions in the relatively small $2 p$-orbitals of $\mathrm{F}$ and thus incoming electrons experience much less attraction. Thus, the correct order is $\mathrm{Cl}\gt \mathrm{F}\gt \mathrm{Br}\gt \mathrm{I}$.

questions.q: The property which is not true about Fluorine is,
options: Most of its reactions are exothermic.
It forms only one oxo acid.
questions.solution:
Most of the reaction of fluorine is exothermic because fluorine in its elemental state is the most electronegative element
in the periodic table. Due to its highest electronegativity, its bond dissociation enthalpy is low. HOF is the only oxoacid of
fluorine.

questions.q: Which is true regarding nitrogen ?
options: Ability to form \( \mathrm{p} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi \) bonds with itself
questions.solution:
Electronic configuration for \( \mathrm{N}(Z=7) \) is \( 1 s^{2} 2 s^{2} 2 p^{3} \), so, it does not have d-orbitals. Due to completely half-filled p-
orbital, its ionization enthalpy is high, and nitrogen is third most electronegative element in periodic table. Nitrogen can
form pII - pII bonds to itself.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options:
Energies of stationary states in hydrogen like atoms is inversely proportional to the square
of the principal quantum number.
The radius of the first orbit of \( \mathrm{He}^{+} \)is half that of the first orbit of hydrogen atom.
Angular quantum number signifies the shape of the orbital.
Total number of nodes for \( 3 \mathrm{~s} \) orbital is three
questions.solution:
The total number of nodes of an orbital is the sum of angular and radial nodes and is given in terms of the $\mathrm{n}$ and $\mathrm{I}$
quantum number by the following equation. Number of nodes $=n-l-1$
for 3 s-orbital, $\mathrm{n}=3\mathrm{I}=0$
Nodes $=3-0-1=2$
Because for s-orbitals, $\mathrm{l}=0$, therefore, there is no angular nodes only radial nodes are present, that is, 2 radial nodes.

Conversion of oxygen into ozone is endothermic process $(\Delta \mathrm{H}=+\mathrm{ve})$ and proceeds through decrease in entropy
$(\Delta \mathrm{S}=-\mathrm{ve})3 \mathrm{O}_{2}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{O}_{3}(g)\Delta \mathrm{G}=\Delta \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}\Delta \mathrm{G}=+\mathrm{ve}$
Therefore, reaction is non-spontaneous at all temperatures

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options:
Van der Waals constant 'a' measures extent of intermolecular attractive forces for real
gases.
Boyle point depends on the nature of real gas,
Compressibility factor measures the deviation of real gas from ideal behaviour.
Critical temperature is the lowest temperature at which liquefaction of a gas first occurs.
questions.solution:
Critical temperature is not the lowest temperature at which liquefaction of a gas first occurs. The critical temperature of a
substance is the temperature at and above which vapor of the substance cannot be liquefied no matter how much
pressure is applied. Therefore, statement (4) is incorrect.
